title: US bond market closed all day for Veterans Day — with NYSE equities trading a full session
source: NEWS: sifma.org/resources/general/holiday-schedule ('Holiday Schedule', SIFMA's own US Holiday Recommendations panel), fetched direct 2026-09-05 (HTTP 200, 298,899 bytes) and parsed out of the page's embedded payload by this session. The US 2026 panel renders holiday/date pairs in sequence and this one reads exactly 'Veterans Day' / 'Wednesday, November 11, 2026', with NO 'Early Close' note attached — the full-closure shape, distinct from the early-close entries elsewhere in the same panel (e.g. 'Thanksgiving Day' / 'Thursday, November 26, 2026' / 'Early Close (2:00 p.m. Eastern Time): Friday, November 27, 2026'). Cross-checked the same day against NYSE nyse.com/markets/hours-calendars (HTTP 200 after its 302, 109,180 bytes, parsed cell-by-cell): its grid states 'All NYSE markets observe U.S. holidays as listed below for 2026, 2027, and 2028' and lists nine holidays per year — New Year's Day, MLK Day, Washington's Birthday, Good Friday, Memorial Day, Juneteenth, Independence Day, Labor Day, Thanksgiving Day, Christmas Day — with ZERO Veterans Day row in any of the three years, so NYSE equities trade a full 09:30-16:00 ET session on 2026-11-11 while the recommended fixed-income tape is dark. Filed estimate on three counts, identical to the three sifma-bond-early-close entries already on this calendar: the confirmed-prefix taxonomy in market-events-data.ts has no slot for an industry trade association's recommended schedule, this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep, and SIFMA's own page states its schedule is a recommendation ('SIFMA recommends a holiday schedule for financial markets in the U.S., U.K. and Japan') rather than a market-wide halt each firm is bound by.
notes: DISCOVERED during the boj-summary-of-opinions-2026-11-10 initial research (2026-09-05), while sweeping that event's +/-5-day corridor for anything dated that the calendar did not already carry. Why it earns a row rather than a footnote: it is the ONLY full-day cross-asset schedule split in the forward window — the three sifma-bond-early-close entries already tracked (2026-12-31, 2027-03-25, 2027-05-28) shorten the bond session by hours, while this one removes it entirely with equities open all day, and the calendar carries no other instance of that shape. And it lands ONE SESSION AFTER a confirmed high-impact CPI print (cpi-2026-11-10, BLS-sourced, 08:30 ET): the cash Treasury market that ordinarily prices the day-after digestion of a CPI surprise is shut on 11-11, so the rates read of that print is deferred to 11-12 while equities trade through it uninterrupted. Anyone reading the 11-11 tape for a rates confirmation of the 11-10 CPI will be reading an equity-only tape and may not notice. STRUCTURAL AND LOW-IMPACT ONLY: a recommended closure moves nothing by itself, no house playbook is calendar- or holiday-keyed, and this widens caution about cross-asset reads on 11-11 while licensing nothing. HONEST LIMITS. (1) The kind field: EventKind (src/domain/market-events-types.ts) has no market-structure member, so this is filed 'rates' — the same choice sifma-bond-early-close-2026-12-31 and sifma-bond-early-close-2027-03-25 already made for the adjacent shape; whether the union needs a 'market-structure' member is not this lane's call. (2) CME futures hours on 11-11 are NOT asserted: cmegroup.com has returned HTTP 403 to this runner across every prior attempt in sibling lanes and this session did not re-attempt it, so the futures leg is unresearched rather than assumed. (3) Whether Treasury moves any 11-11 auction settlement off the closed day is likewise not asserted here — treasurydirect.gov was not fetched by this session.
